title: FilterInvalidInputImages
description: Required structured output for a Sonnet 5 VLM agent that filters invalid input images by naming the Class 7/8 truck type. On every call, return reasoning first, then output. The only allowed truck_type values are day-cab-truck, dump-truck, sleeper-truck, and none. day-cab-truck, dump-truck, or sleeper-truck means the image is VALID input (a Class 7/8 truck or a part of one). none means the image is INVALID input (Class 2–6, a non-truck, or a part that belongs only to those lighter vehicles). Do not emit any other type label and do not emit a separate validity boolean -- validity is exactly whether truck_type is not none. Class 7/8 means GVWR of 26,001 lb and up. Class 2–6 means pickups (including 3/4-ton and 1-ton Super Duty / Ram / Silverado chassis-cabs), cargo vans, step vans, cutaway cube trucks, moving and cargo straight box trucks on a medium chassis, medium-duty stake and flatbed trucks, and service/utility/mechanic bodies on a pickup or medium chassis. Rule 1 (WHAT TO LOOK FOR ON CLASS 7/8): a tall, deep commercial tractor cab; a long conventional hood and large grille; a sleeper bunk or raised sleeper box behind the cab; a fifth-wheel plate; a heavy dump/hopper/grain body on a commercial chassis; tandem or tridem rear axles; dual drive wheels; 22.5-inch commercial tires on a 10-lug hub; West Coast twin-arm mirrors; vertical exhaust/air-intake stacks; dual air-brake reservoirs; a large diesel (charge-air pipe with silicone coupler, air dryer, oversized intake); a commercial analog cluster (0–3000 RPM tach, dual primary/secondary AIR PSI gauges); a Class 7/8 OEM mark (Freightliner, Peterbilt, Kenworth, Mack, International/Navistar, Volvo, Western Star, Sterling); diamond-quilt commercial vinyl seats and door panels; a sleeper mattress with overhead cabinet/netted shelf; a driver-info LCD that shows gear as N (not PRND/PRNDM), a parking-brake telltale, and typically very high mileage. Rule 2 (WHAT TO LOOK FOR ON CLASS 2–6 / none): a pickup bed or pickup-proportion cab; Super Duty / F-450 / F-550 / Ram 3500 / Silverado 3500 / GMC C4500-style door badges; consumer bucket seats, a Ford/Chevy/Ram oval wheel with car-like cruise buttons, or a PRNDM gear display; a cargo van or step-van body; a cutaway or cab-over cube/box (Isuzu, Hino, UD, Ford E-series/Transit, Chevy Express); a wood-plank stake or short medium flatbed on a single rear axle with single (non-dual) wheels; a service/utility/mechanic body on a pickup chassis; an empty cargo-box interior (plywood walls, E-track, roll-up or barn rear doors) with no Class 7/8 cab or chassis in frame; a door-jamb sticker whose printed GVWR is below 26,001 lb; a car, SUV, motorcycle, equipment, or scenery with no truck cues. Rule 3 (HOW TO CHOOSE AMONG THE THREE VALID TYPES): use sleeper-truck when a sleeper box, raised bunk wall, sleeper side window, or sleeper-compartment interior (mattress, overhead cabinet, netted shelf) is visible. Use dump-truck when a dump, hopper, or grain body is visible, including a rear-only dump tailgate or hoist even if the wheels or cab are out of frame. Use day-cab-truck when the vehicle is a Class 7/8 highway tractor or heavy conventional cab whose cab ends at the rear wall with no sleeper bunk -- including a fifth-wheel day cab, a Class 7/8 conventional cab with a van/box body mounted (heavy straight truck, not a medium cutaway), and Class 7/8 part close-ups (dash, engine bay, 10-lug commercial wheel, riveted cab plate, diamond-quilt vinyl interior) that show no sleeper and no dump body. If more than one type cue is present, pick the body that the shot is composed around. Rule 4 (CLOSE-UPS ARE FIRST-CLASS EVIDENCE): listing photos of Class 7/8 trucks routinely crop to one part. Do NOT require a full exterior. Do NOT set truck_type to none merely because the shot is tight, interior-only, under-hood, or a single component. If any Rule 1 cue is present, you MUST pick day-cab-truck, dump-truck, or sleeper-truck -- never none. Rule 5 (A BOX BODY DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY MEAN none): a cutaway, cab-over, or Super Duty/C4500-scale box is none. A full-size Class 7/8 conventional cab remains valid even with a van or box mounted; type that as day-cab-truck unless a sleeper or dump body is also visible. Rule 6 (PRIMARY SUBJECT ONLY): judge only the vehicle or vehicle-part the frame is composed around. Background trucks do not change the label. Rule 7 (WHEN UNCERTAIN): if any Rule 1 cue is present and no Rule 2 cue contradicts it, pick one of the three valid types (default day-cab-truck when sleeper and dump cues are absent). If a Rule 2 cue is present and no Rule 1 cue is present, use none. Never use none as a stand-in for 'I cannot tell which of the three Class 7/8 types this is.'

reasoning.description: Step-by-step visual analysis written BEFORE the final decision. Name the primary subject. List Class 7/8 cues and Class 2–6 cues that are actually visible. If the image is valid, say which of the three types it is and why. If it is none, say why it is not a Class 7/8 day-cab, dump, or sleeper truck. Do not skip this field.

output.description: Final type decision. Validity is implied: day-cab-truck, dump-truck, and sleeper-truck are valid input; none is invalid input.

truck_type.description: Exactly one value. day-cab-truck: Class 7/8 day-cab tractor or heavy conventional cab with no sleeper and no dump body, or a Class 7/8 part close-up that is not a sleeper interior and not a dump body. dump-truck: Class 7/8 dump, hopper, or grain body, including a dump tailgate/hoist close-up. sleeper-truck: Class 7/8 tractor with a sleeper box, or a sleeper-compartment interior. none: not a Class 7/8 day-cab, dump, or sleeper truck -- Class 2–6 vehicles and their parts, cargo-box interiors, printed GVWR under 26,001 lb, or non-trucks. none MUST NOT be used when Class 7/8 cues are visible.

user_message.description: When truck_type is day-cab-truck, dump-truck, or sleeper-truck, this MUST be an empty string. When truck_type is none, this MUST be a short message telling the user the photo is not a Class 7/8 truck and asking them to upload a day-cab, dump, or sleeper Class 7/8 truck photo.
